terms.gloss: a bump, a pimple: the itchy bump a bite leaves
evidence: Levi–Bini p. 16: papula, the little swelling from an insect’s sting
terms.comment: Celsus’s word for a small raised bump on the skin; Levi and Bini give it for the swelling an insect leaves.

terms.gloss: a bite or sting (of an insect or a snake)
evidence: Cic. Off. 2.19: ā bēstiīs ictūs, morsūs, impetūs
terms.comment: The bite itself; Traupman gives it for the bite of a snake or an insect. ictus culicis is a mosquito’s bite.

phrases.latin: Tōtum crūs papulīs opertum est: culicēs mē noctū momordērunt.
phrases.english: My whole leg is covered in bites: the mosquitoes bit me in the night.
Don’t scratch the bite; it’ll itch more.

phrases.latin: Ictūs culicum prūriunt, sed mox abībunt.
phrases.english: Mosquito bites itch, but they’ll soon go away.

sources: Lewis & Short: papula · Lewis & Short: ictus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 280.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 16, s.v. cocciola.
